parts.instruction: Write the correct term or name described.

questions.question: The process of cultivating plants and domesticating animals for food.
The "New Stone Age," associated with settled farming communities.
The ancient civilization located between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers.
The method of supplying water to crops, especially important in ancient Egypt.
The ancient Chinese invention used to determine direction.
The mathematical concept developed in ancient India that is essential to the modern number system.
The Greek philosopher known for systematic observation and classification of living things.
Medieval religious communities that preserved and copied many classical manuscripts.
The Renaissance invention that enabled books and ideas to spread more rapidly.
A systematic process of observing, forming hypotheses, testing, and drawing conclusions.
The inventor whose improvements made the steam engine more efficient during the Industrial Revolution.
The production arrangement in which workers and machines are concentrated in one workplace.
The era marked by the widespread use of computers, digital communication, and information networks.
The social arrangement in which people perform specialized jobs instead of producing everything they need themselves.
The wedge-shaped writing system developed by the Sumerians.
The picture-based writing system used in ancient Egypt.
The Chinese invention that became a widely used material for writing and record-keeping.
The Renaissance intellectual movement that emphasized human dignity, potential, and classical learning.
The study of celestial bodies that helped ancient societies create calendars and predict seasons.
Archaeologists discover a settlement with permanent houses, stored grain, domesticated animals, and specialized crafts. Identify the major historical transformation represented by this evidence.

parts.instruction: Choose the letter of the best answer.

questions.question: A town adopts movable-type printing and soon sees faster sharing of scientific ideas, religious debates, and political opinions. What is the best explanation for this change?

choices.label: a
choices.text: Printing limited knowledge to wealthy families.

choices.label: b
choices.text: Printing made written materials easier to reproduce and circulate.

choices.label: c
choices.text: Printing ended the need for schools and teachers.

choices.label: d
choices.text: Printing was used only for recording taxes.

questions.question: A manufacturer replaces hand production with steam-powered machines and large factories. This change most directly illustrates the:
A Philippine coffee cooperative uses online platforms to sell abroad and joins virtual training with foreign roasters. Which outcome best shows how globalization can support economic growth?

choices.label: a
choices.text: Local producers no longer need skills development.

choices.label: b
choices.text: Producers gain wider markets and access to new knowledge.

choices.label: c
choices.text: All local businesses become independent of foreign competition.

choices.label: d
choices.text: Technology has no effect on trade.

questions.question: A Filipino researcher adapts an imported water-testing device so that local communities can repair it using affordable parts. This is an example of:
Which conclusion about colonial contributions to Philippine science and technology is most accurate?

choices.label: a
choices.text: Colonial periods had no influence on Philippine institutions.

choices.label: b
choices.text: All Philippine technologies were created by colonizers.

choices.label: c
choices.text: Colonial rule introduced some technologies and institutions, which Filipinos later adapted to local needs.

choices.label: d
choices.text: Colonial technologies immediately removed social inequality.

questions.question: Agricultural scientists develop salt-tolerant rice, and extension workers train farmers to use it. Farmers later report more stable harvests and incomes. What does this best demonstrate?

choices.label: a
choices.text: Locally relevant research can contribute to economic development.

choices.label: b
choices.text: Scientific research has no connection to farming.

choices.label: c
choices.text: Farmers should never receive technological training.

choices.label: d
choices.text: Economic development depends only on imported products.

questions.question: A hospital needs an affordable device to help premature infants in low-resource settings. Which Filipino innovator is most closely associated with low-cost infant care equipment?
A community plans to develop electricity from underground heat and steam in a volcanic region. Which Filipino scientist's work is most relevant?

Filipino engineers co-design a low-cost solar dryer with farmers, test it in rural communities, and improve it based on feedback. This approach best shows that national development is supported when technology:

choices.label: b
choices.text: Responds to local needs through collaboration

questions.question: A museum label states that Agapito Flores invented the fluorescent lamp, but historical records show that fluorescent-lamp patents existed earlier. What is the most responsible action for the museum?

choices.label: a
choices.text: Repeat the claim without checking evidence.

choices.label: b
choices.text: Remove all references to Filipino inventors.

choices.label: c
choices.text: Verify primary sources and present the attribution carefully.

choices.label: d
choices.text: Assume every popular story is historically accurate.

questions.question: A coastal town needs official forecasts on rainfall, typhoons, and climate conditions before ordering evacuations. Which agency should it consult?
After an earthquake near an active volcano, officials need information about volcanic activity, fault movement, and possible tsunamis. Which agency is most appropriate?
A government-employed researcher seeks protection for career development, benefits, and working conditions in public science service. Which law is most relevant?
A financially disadvantaged but academically talented student wants support to pursue a degree in engineering. Which law is most closely associated with this type of S&T scholarship?
A policymaker proposes creating a national body to strengthen organized scientific research and development. Which law historically established the National Science Development Board?

A Filipino materials scientist working overseas is invited to conduct short-term research, mentor local researchers, and share expertise with Philippine institutions. Which DOST program best fits this situation?
Which proposed research project is most likely to receive support as a national R&D priority?

choices.label: a
choices.text: A project with no identified problem or intended users

choices.label: b
choices.text: A project that addresses a national need, has a sound method, and involves relevant partners

choices.label: c
choices.text: A project designed only to copy an existing product without improvement

choices.label: d
choices.text: A project that refuses to test its results

questions.question: Which evidence would best show that an early-warning technology program is effective?

choices.label: b
choices.text: The color of the warning-device logo

choices.label: c
choices.text: Faster warnings, wider coverage, and improved community response

choices.label: d
choices.text: The number of speeches made during its launch

questions.question: A student chooses a career not only for income but also because it allows meaningful service, personal growth, and good character. This choice best reflects Aristotle's idea of:
Two learners both receive tablets, but only one has internet access, accessible learning materials, and training. Amartya Sen's capability approach would emphasize that:

choices.label: a
choices.text: Owning the same device guarantees equal opportunity

choices.label: b
choices.text: Real freedom depends on what people are able to do with available resources

choices.label: c
choices.text: Technology should never be used in education

choices.label: d
choices.text: Income is the only measure of well-being

questions.question: Residents jointly create a neighborhood emergency group chat, share verified information, and assist vulnerable neighbors during disasters. This best reflects:
A school wants to know whether a learning app improves students' quality of life. Which evaluation is most appropriate?

choices.label: a
choices.text: Measure only the app's number of downloads.

choices.label: b
choices.text: Consider learning, stress, relationships, access, and student autonomy.

choices.label: d
choices.text: Assume all digital tools improve well-being.

questions.question: A community provides assistive technology, training, and reliable internet to persons with disabilities. This most clearly expands their:

A social-media platform gains revenue by keeping users online as long as possible, even when users report fatigue and reduced face-to-face interaction. What revision would best promote digital well-being?

choices.label: c
choices.text: Give users meaningful controls over notifications and screen-time use.

choices.label: d
choices.text: Make the platform harder to exit.

questions.question: A community makerspace teaches young people to repair devices, share tools, and design projects that solve local problems. Which value is most strongly expressed?

choices.label: d
choices.text: Technology as an end in itself

parts.instruction: Write True if the statement is correct and False if it is incorrect.

questions.question: A barangay app designed through community consultation and shared responsibility reflects Kapwa and bayanihan.
Viewing a forest only in terms of the timber it can supply is an example of enframing.
Heidegger believed that technology is merely a neutral tool with no effect on how people understand the world.
A school that asks how facial-recognition technology may affect trust and privacy is questioning technology rather than accepting it uncritically.
Virtue ethics judges actions only by rules and ignores character.
Using digital tools intentionally to strengthen relationships and reduce unnecessary consumption can support meaningful living.
More screen time automatically leads to greater well-being.
A technology policy that considers human flourishing, virtue, autonomy, community relationships, and environmental effects is a defensible response to technological enframing.
Because technology can shape how people see the world, Heidegger's ideas require society to reject every form of technology.
If genetic engineering is technically successful, it is automatically ethical even when long-term risks and justice concerns are ignored.
An AI hiring system is ethically stronger when it is regularly audited for bias and provides people a way to question decisions.
Replacing all human interaction in elder care with robots is automatically ethical if it lowers costs.
Ethical evaluation of gene editing should consider safety, informed consent, fairness, and possible effects on future generations.
If only wealthy people can access enhancement technologies, concerns about justice and inequality may arise.
Posthumanism always rejects human dignity and ethical responsibility.
Making an AI system more transparent can improve accountability, although transparency alone may not solve every ethical problem.
A highly accurate surveillance system may ignore privacy and consent because good performance is the only ethical standard.
Responsible development of robotics should include safety testing, human oversight, and consideration of effects on workers and communities.
A cognitive-enhancement technology is automatically ethical as long as adults voluntarily choose to use it.
Governments should create adaptable safeguards for emerging technologies by considering benefits, risks, rights, and public participation.
